The angles ${30}^{∘}$ and ${45}^{∘}$ are special, and their trigonometric ratios have the  values

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡{30}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3},\,\operatorname{tan}⁡{45}^{∘}=1.
$$

Also, note that ${tan}^{2}⁡{30}^{∘}$ simply means $(\operatorname{tan}⁡{30}^{∘})^{2}.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}3{tan}^{2}⁡{30}^{∘}-\operatorname{tan}⁡{45}^{∘} & = \\ 3{(\operatorname{tan}⁡{30}^{∘})}^{2}-\operatorname{tan}⁡{45}^{∘} & = \\ 3{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})}^{2}-1 & = \\ 3(\frac{3}{9})-1 & = \\ 1-1 & = \\ 0 & .\end{aligned}
$$

The angles ${45}^{∘},$ ${30}^{∘}$ and ${0}^{∘}$ are special angles, and their trigonometric ratios have the values

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡{45}^{∘}=1,\,\operatorname{tan}⁡{30}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3},\,\operatorname{tan}⁡{0}^{∘}=0.
$$

Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡{45}^{∘}+\operatorname{tan}⁡{30}^{∘}+\operatorname{tan}⁡{0}^{∘} & = \\ 1+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}+0 & = \\ \frac{3+\sqrt{3}}{3}. & \end{aligned}
$$
